title: Noise is not the same as action
literal_meaning: The cloud that thunders does not rain.
explanation: The contrast between loud thunder and absent rain is used to question bluster: impressive promises or threats do not necessarily lead to action. Read the sentence figuratively. Thunderstorms can, of course, bring rain; the proverb is not a dependable weather rule.
meaning_odia: ମେଘର ଗର୍ଜନ ବଡ଼, କିନ୍ତୁ ବର୍ଷାର ଦେଖା ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ତଫାତକୁ ମଣିଷର କଥା ଓ କାମ ସହ ମେଳାଯାଇଛି। ବହୁତ ଘୋଷଣା ବା ଧମକ ଥାଇ କାମରେ କିଛି ନଦିଶିଲେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଏ। ଗର୍ଜନର ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗକୁ ଜୋର୍ ଦିଏ; ସବୁ ମେଘ ବିଷୟରେ ନିୟମ ଦେଉନାହିଁ।
usage_example: Someone loudly promises to repair a shared bench, but nothing happens. Others use the saying to ask for action rather than another announcement. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Weather becomes a way of talking about human speech. Similar imagery elsewhere would not by itself prove where this Odia wording originated.

odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ବଡ଼ କଥା କହିବା ଓ କାମ କରିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: Loud promises or threats need not lead to action; the thundercloud is a metaphor, not a weather rule.
